title: Inkline — collaborative editing
description: Panels chosen for the questions one has to be able to answer about THIS system, rather than for a list of 'what people usually measure'. Every row carries a description saying what a bad value means.

panels.title: Latencja serwerowa operacji (p50 / p95 / p99)
panels.description: Operation intake -> broadcast to this instance's clients. ONE clock, so the only latency whose number can be quoted without caveats. Client-to-client latency is measured solely in the benchmark harness (CP8) and is NOT here — deliberately, because it would require comparing two different clocks.

panels.title: Czas scalenia CRDT (p95)
panels.description: The algorithm alone, without transport or persistence. This is where the difference between an O(n) and an O(log n) index shows — a value growing with document size means the indexing structure has stopped keeping up.

panels.title: Active sessions and in-memory documents
panels.description: The number of in-memory documents matters, because ADR-0004 deliberately multiplies memory use by the number of instances holding the same document.

panels.title: Operacje bez przyczyny
panels.description: Operations waiting for their origin. Transient values > 0 are normal (the network reorders). A value that STAYS above zero means a permanently missing operation, that is, a corrupt log — see ADR-0004.

panels.title: Gap repairs in the numbering (messages lost by Redis)
panels.description: ADR-0004: Redis pub/sub loses messages, and that is expected rather than exceptional. NOTE — a permanently zero value is NOT good news: it means the repair mechanism has never fired, so there is no telling whether it works at all. The CP8 chaos test triggers it on purpose.

panels.title: Tombstone share
panels.description: Characters deleted but still present in the structure. A monotonically rising value means GC is not working — usually because one hung client is blocking causal stability for the whole document (ADR-0005). Note: even a working GC will not reach zero, because a tombstone in the middle of the text is the origin of the next block and must not be removed.

panels.title: Operacje odrzucone (RESYNC_REQUIRED)
panels.description: Clients offline for longer than the GC window whose changes could not be merged (ADR-0005). Every such event means a user who saw the recovered-draft message — a real, if controlled, inconvenience.

panels.title: Are the clients keeping up with the broadcasts
Session disconnects by reason
panels.description: This panel exists to close an open question in the README (the 'Degradation point' section): why, above ~10 clients in one document, some of them fall permanently behind even though the server holds the complete set of operations. The BAD VALUE is a rising slow_client_buffer_overflow — the client cannot keep up with delivery, its send queue exceeds send-buffer-size-bytes (ADR-0002), and the server tears down its session. The client comes back through reconnect+resync, so from the outside it looks like a brief hiccup rather than lost deliveries. If this series grows with the client count, the bottleneck is BROADCASTING rather than CRDT merging. NOTE: a permanently zero value while clients are diverging does NOT mean all is well — it means the cause lies elsewhere and the hypothesis has to be rejected.
